name: Amazonas

sources.name: Departamento Administrativo Nacional de Estadística (DANE), Censo Nacional de Población y Vivienda 2018, Autoreconocimiento étnico, prepared as subnational tables by the U.S. Census Bureau

ethnicity_note:
2018 census, self-reported ethnicity (autoreconocimiento étnico). The seven categories sum to 44,164,417, which is the sheet's own published universe of people who answered the question, against a counted population of about 48 million. Colombia's census asks which of five recognised groups a person recognises themselves in -- indigenous, Rrom/gypsy, raizal, palenquero, black or Afro-Colombian -- so "No ethnic group" at 87.6% is an answer people gave, not a residual this build invented. That 87.6% is predominantly mestizo and white Colombians, who are the majority of the country and are not among the five groups the question offers; the census does not count them separately, so this map does not either. The category is left under the name the census gave it rather than renamed to one it never asked about.

The same workbook carries a second sheet naming 124 individual indigenous peoples, and it is not read. Its universe is the 1,905,617 people who said they were indigenous, not the country, so published as Colombia's ethnicity it would reconcile perfectly and tell a reader Colombia is 100% indigenous.

That 87.6% is predominantly mestizo and white Colombians, who are the majority of the country and are not among the five groups the question offers; the census does not count them separately, so this map does not either. The category is left under the name the census gave it rather than renamed to one it never asked about.

The same workbook carries a second sheet naming 124 individual indigenous peoples, and it is not read. Its universe is the 1,905,617 people who said they were indigenous, not the country, so published as Colombia's ethnicity it would reconcile perfectly and tell a reader Colombia is 100% indigenous.
